title: All the angles that work
objectives: Solve a trigonometric equation and find every solution in an interval
Use symmetry for the second solution and the period for the rest
Solve equations in $2x$ and quadratics in $\sin x$

screens.prose: A calculator gives $\sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30^\circ$, so $x = 30^\circ$ solves $\sin x = 0.5$. The dashed line is the height 0.5. Is 30° the only answer between 0° and 360°?
screens.question: Drag the point along the curve to another $x$ between 0° and 360° where $\sin x = 0.5$.

hints.text: Follow the curve past its peak. Where does it come back down to the line?
The curve rises to 1 at 90°, then falls again.
The curve is symmetric about its peak at 90°. 30° is 60° before the peak, so look 60° after it.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find a second place where the curve meets the dashed line.

byKey.start: That is the calculator's answer, where the point began. Find a second crossing further right.
byKey.below: There the curve is below the axis, so $\sin x$ is negative. The line $y = 0.5$ is above the axis.
byKey.top: Near 90° the curve is above the line, with $\sin x$ up to 1. Keep going until it comes back down to 0.5.
byKey.p: The point is not on the line yet. Move it to where the curve crosses the dashed line.

explain.text: The curve crosses the line twice between 0° and 360°: at 30° and at 150°. The calculator gives only the first. The curve is symmetric about its peak at 90°, so the second is $180^\circ - 30^\circ$.

screens.prose: Slide the level $k$. The two dots mark where $\sin x = k$ between 0° and 360°, and the caption reads their positions.
screens.question: What do the two crossings always add up to, in degrees?

hints.text: Set $k$ to 0.5, then 0.8. Add the two numbers in the caption each time.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the two positions in the caption, for two different levels.

byKey.period: 360° is a full turn, the gap between repeats. Add the two crossings in the caption instead.
byKey.quarter: 90° is where the peak sits, halfway between the crossings. The two crossings add to twice that.

explain.text: For $k = 0.8$ the crossings are 53.1° and 126.9°, and they add to 180°. The curve is symmetric about its peak at 90°. So once you have one solution $x_1$, the other is $180^\circ - x_1$.

screens.prose: The calculator's answer, $\sin^{-1} k$, is the **principal value**. The second solution is $180^\circ$ minus it. Solve $\sin x = 0.8$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$. The calculator gives $\sin^{-1}(0.8) = 53.13^\circ$.
screens.question: What is the other solution? Give two decimal places.

hints.text: Which way along the axis is the second crossing: before 180° or after it?
The second crossing is on the falling side of the first hump.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract the principal value from 180°.

byKey.plus: You added 180°. There the curve is below the axis: $\sin 233.13^\circ = -0.8$.
byKey.cosrule: You used $360^\circ - 53.13^\circ$, which is the cosine's mirror. $\sin 306.87^\circ = -0.8$.
byKey.same: That is the principal value again. The question asks for the other one.

explain.text: The second crossing sits as far before 180° as the first sits after 0°. So it is $180^\circ - 53.13^\circ = 126.87^\circ$.

screens.prose: Now solve $\sin x = -0.5$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$. The calculator gives $\sin^{-1}(-0.5) = -30^\circ$, which is outside the interval.
screens.question: Select all that apply. Which values solve the equation in the interval?

options.why: That is the calculator's answer, but it is below 0°. Add 360° to bring it into the interval: 330°.
$\sin 150^\circ = +0.5$. You dropped the minus sign.

hints.text: Where is the curve at height −0.5?
The curve dips below the axis between 180° and 360°.
Symmetry: $180^\circ - (-30^\circ) = 210^\circ$. A full turn: $-30^\circ + 360^\circ = 330^\circ$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find both places in the interval where the curve sits at −0.5.

byKey.m30: −30° is the calculator's value, but the interval starts at 0°. A full turn moves it to 330°.
byKey.a150: At 150° the curve is at +0.5, above the axis. The equation needs −0.5.

explain.text: Symmetry gives $180^\circ - (-30^\circ) = 210^\circ$. Adding a full turn to the principal value gives $330^\circ$. Both sit where the curve dips to −0.5.

screens.prose: Widen the interval. Solve $\sin x = 0.5$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 720^\circ$, two full turns of the circle.
screens.question: Select all that apply. Which values solve the equation?

options.why: That is $360^\circ - 30^\circ$, the cosine's mirror. $\sin 330^\circ = -0.5$.
$\sin 750^\circ = 0.5$, but 750° is past the end of the interval, 720°.

hints.text: The curve repeats after a full turn. How far apart are the repeats?
The second wave is the first moved 360° to the right.
Add 360° to 30° and to 150°. Adding it again passes 720°.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find both solutions in the first turn, then add 360° to each.

byKey.a330: 330° comes from the cosine's mirror. On the sine curve it sits at −0.5.
byKey.a750: 750° solves the equation, but the interval stops at 720°.

explain.text: A full turn of 360° brings the point back, so the curve repeats. 30° and 150° give 390° and 510°. The next pair starts at 750°, past the end.

screens.prose: Cosine next. Solve $\cos x = 0.5$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$. The calculator gives $\cos^{-1}(0.5) = 60^\circ$.
screens.question: Drag the point to the other solution.

hints.text: Where is the cosine curve lowest? The curve is symmetric about that point.
The cosine curve is lowest at 180°, so it mirrors about 180°.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the second place the cosine curve meets the line.

byKey.sinrule: You used the sine's mirror, $180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$. The cosine curve is at −0.5 there.
byKey.start: That is the calculator's answer, where the point began. Look on the right of the trough.
byKey.p: The point is not on the line yet. Move it to where the curve rises back through the dashed line.

explain.text: The cosine curve is symmetric about 180°, not 90°. So the second solution is $360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ$. On the circle, 300° mirrors 60° in the horizontal axis, keeping the across-distance.

screens.prose: Tangent. Solve $\tan x = 1$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$. The calculator gives $\tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ$.
screens.question: What is the other solution, in degrees?

hints.text: How far apart are the branches of the tangent curve?
The tangent curve repeats every 180°, not every 360°.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The tangent repeats every 180°: add that to the principal value.

explain.text: The tangent curve repeats every 180°, so the solutions are 45° and 225°. At 225° the sine and cosine are both negative, and their ratio is +1.

screens.prose: Solve $\sin 2x = 0.5$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$. The graph shows the familiar $y = \sin x$, for reference.
screens.question: How many solutions are there?

hints.text: Let $u = 2x$. As $x$ runs from 0° to 360°, where does $u$ run?
$u$ runs from 0° to 720°: two full turns.
$\sin u = 0.5$ for $u = 30^\circ, 150^\circ, 390^\circ, 510^\circ$. Halve each to get $x$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Solve for $u = 2x$ over the whole range $u$ covers, then halve.

byKey.two: You counted solutions of $\sin x = 0.5$. As $x$ runs to 360°, $2x$ runs to 720°: two turns, so twice the solutions.
byKey.one: You kept only the calculator's value. Symmetry gives a second, and the doubled angle gives two more.
byKey.eight: You doubled the range twice. $2x$ runs to 720°, which holds four solutions of $\sin u = 0.5$, not eight.

explain.text: Put $u = 2x$, so $u$ runs from 0° to 720°. Then $u = 30^\circ, 150^\circ, 390^\circ, 510^\circ$, and $x$ is half of each. The graph of $\sin 2x$ squeezes two waves into 360°, so it meets the line four times.

screens.prose: Some equations are quadratics in disguise. In $2\sin^2 x - \sin x - 1 = 0$, put $s = \sin x$: $$2s^2 - s - 1 = (2s + 1)(s - 1) = 0.$$
screens.question: Select all that apply. Which $x$ between 0° and 360° solve it?

options.why: That solves $\sin x = 0.5$. The factor $2s + 1 = 0$ gives $s = -0.5$, with a minus.
$\sin 270^\circ = -1$. The factors give $s = 1$ and $s = -0.5$, not −1.

hints.text: Each factor gives one value of $s$. Solve $\sin x = 1$ and $\sin x = -0.5$ separately.
$\sin x = 1$ only at the very top of the wave.
$\sin x = 1$ gives 90° only. $\sin x = -0.5$ gives 210° and 330°.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Solve $\sin x = 1$ and $\sin x = -0.5$, then list every angle.

byKey.a270: At 270° the sine is −1, and neither factor gives −1.

explain.text: The factor $s - 1$ gives $\sin x = 1$. The line $y = 1$ only touches the top of the wave, so there is one solution, 90°. The factor $2s + 1$ gives $\sin x = -0.5$: 210° and 330°.

screens.prose: Let $x_1$ be the calculator's value. Then $$\begin{aligned} \sin x = k&: \quad x_1,\ 180^\circ - x_1 \\ \cos x = k&: \quad x_1,\ 360^\circ - x_1 \\ \tan x = k&: \quad x_1,\ x_1 + 180^\circ \end{aligned}$$ After that, add or subtract whole periods until you leave the interval: 360°, or 180° for tangent.
screens.question: Which list solves $\cos x = -0.5$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$?

options.why: You used the sine's mirror, $180^\circ - 120^\circ$. $\cos 60^\circ = +0.5$.
That is the calculator's value alone. The cosine curve meets the line a second time.
Those solve $\cos x = +0.5$. You dropped the minus sign.

hints.text: The calculator gives $\cos^{-1}(-0.5) = 120^\circ$. Which rule gives the second?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use the cosine's mirror on the calculator's value.

explain.text: The calculator gives 120°, and the cosine's mirror gives $360^\circ - 120^\circ = 240^\circ$. Both sit where the curve dips to −0.5.

screens.prose: Now justify the full list for $\sin x = 0.5$ on $0^\circ \le x \le 720^\circ$. Each line gives its reason.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: $x = 30^\circ$ is one solution, the principal value $\sin^{-1}(0.5)$
$\sin(180^\circ - x) = \sin x$, the mirror in the vertical axis, so $150^\circ$ is another
$\sin(x + 360^\circ) = \sin x$, since a full turn returns the point, so $390^\circ$ and $510^\circ$ also work
One more turn passes $720^\circ$, so the list is complete: $30^\circ, 150^\circ, 390^\circ, 510^\circ$

hints.text: Start with the one solution you can get without any reasoning.
Use the symmetry before the period: you need both solutions in the first turn.
Principal value, then symmetry, then a full turn, then check the end of the interval.

feedback.correct: Principal value, symmetry, period, then the end of the interval.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Begin with the calculator's value.

byKey.d3: Add the period to both first-turn solutions, so the symmetry line comes before it.
byKey.d4: Checking the end of the interval comes last, once every candidate is listed.

explain.text: The symmetry gives the second solution in the first turn. The period copies both into the next turn. Checking the interval's end stops the list, which is where most missing answers come from.

screens.prose: Two seasonal premiums, in £ per MWh: gas $4\sin\big(\tfrac{\pi t}{6}\big)$ and power $4\cos\big(\tfrac{\pi t}{6}\big)$, with $t$ in months and the angle in radians. A spread trader watches for the times they are equal. Dividing by the cosine gives $\tan\big(\tfrac{\pi t}{6}\big) = 1$.
screens.question: When do the premiums cross for the second time in the year? Give $t$ in months.

hints.text: Solve $\tan u = 1$ for $u = \tfrac{\pi t}{6}$, with $u$ from 0 to $2\pi$ over the year.
The tangent repeats every half turn, $\pi$ radians.
$u = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$ or $\tfrac{5\pi}{4}$. Then $t = \tfrac{6u}{\pi}$: $t = 1.5$ or $t = 7.5$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Solve the tangent equation for the angle, then turn it into a time.

byKey.first: That is the first crossing, from the calculator's $\tfrac{\pi}{4}$. Add the tangent's period, $\pi$, for the second.
byKey.sinrule: You used $\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{4}$, the sine's mirror. Its tangent is $-1$.
byKey.cosrule: You used $2\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{4}$, the cosine's mirror. Its tangent is $-1$.

explain.text: $\tfrac{\pi t}{6} = \tfrac{\pi}{4}$ or $\tfrac{5\pi}{4}$, so $t = 1.5$ or $7.5$; the next, $\tfrac{9\pi}{4}$, is past 12 months. Dividing by the cosine was safe. Where it is 0, at $t = 3$ and $t = 9$, the gas premium is ±4, so they differ.

ideas: The calculator gives one solution, the principal value. Symmetry gives a second in the same turn.
The period copies them: add or subtract 360° (180° for tangent) until you leave the interval.
For $\sin 2x = k$, solve for $u = 2x$ over the whole range $u$ covers, then halve.

formula.name: Second solutions
formula.note: Then add multiples of $360^\circ$ ($180^\circ$ for tangent), and stop at the interval's end.

summary.trap: One calculator answer is not the whole solution. Count the turns the angle makes across the interval.

quiz.prose: Solve $\cos x = -0.5$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$. The calculator gives $120^\circ$.
quiz.question: Which list is complete?

options.why: You used $180^\circ - 120^\circ$, the sine's mirror. $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$.
300° is $360^\circ - 60^\circ$, built from the acute angle. $\cos 300^\circ = +0.5$.
That is the calculator's value alone. Cosine gives a second solution by symmetry.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use the cosine's mirror, $360^\circ - x_1$.

explain.text: The cosine curve is symmetric about 180°. So with $x_1 = 120^\circ$ the second solution is $360^\circ - 120^\circ = 240^\circ$.

quiz.prose: Solve $\tan x = -1$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$. The calculator gives $-45^\circ$.
quiz.question: Which list is complete?

options.why: Those solve $\tan x = +1$. You dropped the minus sign.
−45° is outside the interval. Add 180° twice: 135° and 315°.
The tangent repeats every 180°, so 315° works too.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the tangent's period, 180°, until you leave the interval.

explain.text: Start at $-45^\circ$ and add 180°: 135°, then 315°. Adding again gives 495°, past 360°.

options.why: You took only $\sin x = 0.5$. The square root of 0.25 is $\pm 0.5$, so $\sin x = -0.5$ counts too.
One is the calculator's value for one root. Each root has two solutions in a turn.
Each of $\sin x = 0.5$ and $\sin x = -0.5$ has two solutions in one turn, not four.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take both square roots, then solve each.

explain.text: $\sin x = \pm 0.5$. The positive root gives 30° and 150°; the negative root gives 210° and 330°.

quiz.prose: Solve $\sin x = 0.5$ for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$, with $x$ in radians. The calculator gives $\tfrac{\pi}{6}$.
quiz.question: Which list is complete?

options.why: You mixed units. In radians a half turn is $\pi$, so the second solution is $\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{6}$.
$2\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{6}$ is the cosine's mirror. Its sine is $-0.5$.
You added a half turn. $\sin\tfrac{7\pi}{6} = -0.5$, below the axis.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use the sine's mirror with a half turn of $\pi$.

explain.text: In radians 180° is $\pi$, so the sine's mirror gives $\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{6} = \tfrac{5\pi}{6}$. The period is $2\pi$, so the next pair is past the interval.

options.text: There are none: a sine never exceeds 1

options.why: At 90° the sine is 1, its largest value. It never reaches 1.5.
Symmetry pairs up crossings, but the line $y = 1.5$ never meets the curve.
A calculator reports an error for this. No angle has a sine of 1.5.

feedback.correct: A sine is a height on the unit circle, so it stays between −1 and 1.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask how high the point on the unit circle can go.

explain.text: The sine is a height on a circle of radius 1, so it lies between −1 and 1. The line $y = 1.5$ misses the curve, and there is no solution.
